chunks: Abd al-Malik ibn Umar narrated from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the divorce of the insane person who has lost their intellect; is it valid? He said: No. And about the woman if she is like that; is her sale and her dowry valid? He said: No.

key_terms.الزَّائِلِ الْعَقْلِ: One who has lost their intellect/reason
key_terms.الْمَعْتُوه: The insane person (one suffering from insanity)
key_terms.بَيْعُهَا: Her sale (referring to legal capacity to sell property)

ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of an insane person valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the divorce of a mentally incapacitated person (majtuh) is invalid due to the lack of conscious intent, a ruling that extends to the validity of their sale and dowry. This establishes a parallel between personal status acts and commercial transactions for those lacking full intellectual capacity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on 'aql' (intellect) as a prerequisite for legal agency (ahliyyah).
